newsitem.title: FRANCE: LVMH still working on three-way merger.
newsitem.headline: LVMH still working on three-way merger.

text.p: French luxury goods and drinks group LVMH Moet Hennessy Louis Vuitton said on Tuesday that it was still working on a plan for a three-way merger with Guinness and GrandMet.
LVMH chairman Bernard Arnault will give a detailed written proposal to Guinness chairman Tony Greener and GrandMet head George Bull before the end of the week.

"LVMH is still working on the hypothesis of a three-way marriage," a company spokeswoman said, reacting to a report in the Daily Telegraph newspaper on Saturday and the La Tribune Desfosses paper on Tuesday which said LVMH could swap its cognac for champagne with Guinness.
The newspapers said LVMH could sell its 66 percent stake in the cognac business, including Hennessy, and buy Guinness' 34 percent in the champagne business, which includes the Moet et Chnadon brand.
The papers said that LVMH would keep its worldwide distribution contracts and would also obtain a seat on the board of GMG -- the planned 24-billion-stg merger by Guinness and GrandMet.

Arnault wants to merge his wine and spirits business with those of the two British companies into a separately listed company. Under the original plan, this would exclude LVMH's luxury goods and the British companies' food businesses.
LVMH had no comment on Friday on a report it would have dropped its demand that the food business -- such as Burger King -- be excluded from the venture.
The Breton entrepreneur is one of the biggest investors in both of the other companies.
He has bought some 6.4 percent in GrandMet for over eight billion francs since mid-June on top of LVMH's 14.2 percent stake in Guinness.

Guinness and GrandMet announced their merger in May and Arnault immediately signalled his opposition. Greener and Bull came to Paris on July 3 to listed to Arnault's proposal and they asked him to give written details.
On Tuesday, LVMH was down 0.06 percent at 1,570 francs at 0852 GMT while the blue-chip CAC-40 index was 0.61 percent higher.
